answer: Each new key freezes a bond in a glacier vault that thaws only after several epochs of live work. During the freeze, the network sends irregular zephyr probes — brief, privately seeded questions at uneven times — and records reply timing and wording as a signal fingerprint. Keys whose signals match in phrasing or lockstep timing are treated as one actor and the glacier bond is burned. A farm must lock a separate glacier bond per key and keep a distinct mind awake for every zephyr probe, since one operator cannot emit many independent live signals.
